title: Grade 6 Science — Wed, May 27
description: Components of Food — Day 3 of 5: Balanced diet and functions
subject: science

questions.question: What is a balanced diet?
options: A diet with lots of one nutrient
A diet that contains all nutrients in the right proportions for good health
A diet only for weight loss
A diet with equal amounts of all foods
questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and fibre — each in the right amount for your age and activity level.

questions.question: Carbohydrates should make up the LARGEST portion of a balanced diet because:
options: They are the body's primary and most immediate energy source
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the main fuel for body cells, especially the brain and muscles. They should be about 50-60% of daily calories.

questions.question: Why do athletes need more protein in their diet than non-athletes?
options: Protein gives faster energy for sports
Protein is needed for building and repairing muscles that are stressed during exercise
questions.explanation: Exercise breaks down muscle fibres. Protein provides amino acids needed to repair and build stronger muscles.

questions.question: Why do growing children need MORE protein per kilogram of body weight than adults?
options: Growth requires building new cells and tissues, which needs more protein
questions.explanation: Children are constantly building new muscle, bone, and other tissues. This requires large amounts of protein for new cell construction.

questions.question: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are different from water-soluble vitamins because:
options: They are stored in body fat and liver (not lost daily)
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in fatty tissues and liver. Water-soluble vitamins (B, C) cannot be stored and must be consumed regularly.

questions.question: Which nutrient provides LONG-TERM energy storage in the body?
questions.explanation: Fats stored in adipose (fat) tissue provide long-term energy reserve. The body uses them when carbohydrate stores run low.

questions.question: A person eats only rice and nothing else for months. Which deficiency would develop FIRST?
questions.explanation: Rice is mostly starch. A rice-only diet lacks proteins (muscle wasting), vitamins (scurvy, beriberi), and other nutrients.

questions.question: Dietary fibre is important even though the body cannot digest it because:
options: It adds bulk to stool and stimulates healthy bowel movement, preventing constipation
questions.explanation: Insoluble fibre absorbs water and adds bulk to faeces, making it easier to pass. This prevents constipation and reduces risk of bowel diseases.

questions.question: Why do people living in cold climates need more fat in their diet?
options: Fat provides insulation (under the skin) that keeps the body warm in cold temperatures
They have less access to other foods
questions.explanation: Subcutaneous fat acts as insulation, preventing heat loss from the body. In cold climates, more fat is needed for warmth.

questions.question: The amount of food energy is measured in:
questions.explanation: Food energy is measured in Calories (kcal) or kilojoules (kJ). 1 kcal = 1 food Calorie = 4.18 kJ.

questions.question: Phosphorus is important for which body part?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus combines with calcium in bones and teeth (calcium phosphate). It is also part of ATP (energy molecules) and DNA.

questions.question: Potassium and sodium (electrolytes) are minerals important for:
options: Nerve signal transmission and fluid balance in the body
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium ions are essential for nerve impulses and muscle contractions. They also regulate fluid balance inside and outside cells.

questions.question: Which food is an excellent source of iron for preventing anaemia?
questions.explanation: Green vegetables (spinach) and meat (especially liver, red meat) are good iron sources. Iron is needed to make haemoglobin.

questions.question: Why does the body need water every day (and cannot store much)?
options: Water is continuously lost through urine, sweat, breath, and must be replenished
questions.explanation: The body loses 2-3 litres of water daily through urine, sweat, and breathing. It must be replaced to prevent dehydration.

questions.question: A growing 12-year-old's balanced plate should include:
options: Half whole grains + one-quarter protein + one-quarter vegetables + dairy + fruit
questions.explanation: A healthy plate: ~50% carbohydrates (grains), ~25% proteins (dal, egg, fish), ~25% vegetables, plus fruits and dairy. This ensures all nutrients.
